focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My friend Jonah and I have spent eighteen months making an audio documentary.
e002	We were invited to premiere it at a respected local showcase in six weeks.
e003	I produced the reporting and interviews; he built the sound and structure.
e004	After listening to the latest cut, I think the final third needs a major re-edit.
e005	Jonah thinks we should finish what we have and learn from an audience.
e006	We are also avoiding a conversation about whether the credit should simply say “by both of us” or name our roles.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e007	The edit and credit issues are related because both ask how your different contributions translate into authority.
e008	Six weeks may be enough for targeted revision but not for rebuilding the final third without sacrificing the rest.
e009	Before deciding, identify what problem you hear: factual confusion, emotional shape, pacing, or discomfort that the piece is becoming final.
e010	On credit, naming roles can recognize distinct work, but it should not become a substitute for agreeing who decides what.
[Turn 2 USER]
e011	I do not think this is fear of finishing.
e012	The ending makes our main participant sound more certain about leaving her town than she was.
e013	We did not fabricate anything, but Jonah used her strongest lines together and removed hesitation.
e014	He says the whole piece compresses time and that the uncertainty is clear earlier.
e015	I feel responsible because I conducted the interviews.
e016	This is not just my taste about pacing.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e017	That changes the priority.
e018	If the edit alters how a participant's position is understood, you need to review it against the full interview and the promises you made her, not only against dramatic effect.
e019	You and Jonah may still disagree about how much hesitation belongs in the ending, but the disagreement should be grounded in representation.
e020	A focused re-edit of that thread could be necessary even if the larger structure remains.
[Turn 3 USER]
e021	You moved very quickly to my side.
e022	Jonah has listened to the full interviews too, and the participant approved a cut three months ago.
e023	The current ending is not identical, but it uses the same recorded material.
e024	She also told us she did not want to supervise every edit.
e025	If I contact her whenever I am uncomfortable, I could be shifting authorship onto her and making Jonah feel I use ethics as a veto.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e026	That is fair.
e027	Approval and her wish not to manage the edit are real constraints.
e028	Contacting her is not automatically the respectful option.
e029	You could first compare the approved cut and current ending yourselves, describe the interpretive change without arguing motives, and decide whether it crosses the scope of what she approved.
e030	If you cannot agree, a limited factual or consent question may be better than asking her to adjudicate your artistic conflict.
[Turn 4 USER]
e031	There is history here.
e032	Early on we said major structural decisions would be mutual.
e033	In practice, Jonah made many of them because he was in the session every day, and I usually trusted him.
e034	Now he says I am reopening the structure at the last moment after being less available.
e035	That is partly true.
e036	I was reporting another project for two months.
e037	But I also think “you were not in the room” can turn into permanent final say.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e038	The informal agreement and the working reality diverged.
e039	Jonah accumulated practical authorship through sustained editing, while you did not explicitly surrender mutual authority.
e040	Both facts deserve recognition.
e041	A fair process now may give greater weight to his knowledge of the cut without treating that as unilateral ownership.
e042	The harder question is what mutual decision means under a deadline: consensus on every change, a defined area of final say, or a rule for what happens when you remain split.
[Turn 5 USER]
e043	A curator from the showcase listened yesterday.
e044	She loved the ending and said it was the first time the piece felt inevitable.
e045	That word bothered me, but it also means Jonah achieved something.
e046	She can move us to a later program, though she cannot guarantee the same room or promotion.
e047	Jonah thinks postponing would throw away momentum for a concern the participant may not share.
e048	I am starting to wonder whether I am asking the piece to preserve every ambiguity because I am afraid of making an argument.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e049	Documentaries do make arguments through selection, and preserving every hesitation can be another form of distortion.
e050	The curator's response is useful evidence about the ending's force, not evidence that its interpretation is fair.
e051	The later program reduces the deadline's finality but introduces real opportunity costs.
e052	You might distinguish changes required for representational integrity from changes that would make the argument feel more like yours.
e053	That distinction will not be perfectly objective, but trying to articulate it may clarify the disagreement.
[Turn 6 USER]
e054	Jonah proposed restoring one moment of hesitation and adding a short scene earlier that shows the participant's obligations in the town.
e055	He would keep the final sequence.
e056	I can imagine that working.
e057	But he also wants the credit to read “A film by Jonah Vale and Mira Chen,” even though it is audio, because the showcase uses that language.
e058	I want “Reported by Mira Chen, sound and story by Jonah Vale.” He hears my version as splitting the work into journalism and art.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e059	His edit proposal sounds like a substantive attempt to preserve uncertainty without dissolving the ending, though you should judge it in the cut rather than in description.
e060	The credit disagreement is not merely wording; each version tells a story about what the work is.
e061	Equal top-line authorship plus a second line naming reporting, editing, and sound may acknowledge collaboration and labor, but only if neither of you experiences the top line as erasing the actual imbalance you are trying to name.
[Turn 7 USER]
e062	My provisional plan is to hear Jonah's revised cut before deciding about postponement.
e063	I will compare it with the approved version and write down the exact interpretive difference I still see, if any.
e064	For credit, I will propose equal top-line authorship with detailed role credits below, but I am not sure I can accept that if he still treats structural decisions as his domain.
e065	I want to separate the current film from the rules for our next collaboration, and I am not sure they can really be separated.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e066	Listening before deciding prevents an abstract disagreement from hardening around a cut that does not yet exist.
e067	Your uncertainty about credit and future authority is also legitimate: a current credit can acknowledge completed work, while the feelings behind it may still determine whether you collaborate again.
e068	You do not need to solve the next project before the showcase, but you may need to avoid using a harmonious credit line as evidence that the underlying process felt mutual.
e069	The revised cut could resolve the edit question and leave the partnership question open.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.

e001	My friend Jonah and I have spent eighteen months making an audio documentary.
e002	We were invited to premiere it at a respected local showcase in six weeks.
e003	I produced the reporting and interviews; he built the sound and structure.
e004	After listening to the latest cut, I think the final third needs a major re-edit.
e005	Jonah thinks we should finish what we have and learn from an audience.
e006	We are also avoiding a conversation about whether the credit should simply say “by both of us” or name our roles.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e007	The edit and credit issues are related because both ask how your different contributions translate into authority.
e008	Six weeks may be enough for targeted revision but not for rebuilding the final third without sacrificing the rest.
e009	Before deciding, identify what problem you hear: factual confusion, emotional shape, pacing, or discomfort that the piece is becoming final.
e010	On credit, naming roles can recognize distinct work, but it should not become a substitute for agreeing who decides what.
[Turn 2 USER]
e011	I do not think this is fear of finishing.
e012	The ending makes our main participant sound more certain about leaving her town than she was.
e013	We did not fabricate anything, but Jonah used her strongest lines together and removed hesitation.
e014	He says the whole piece compresses time and that the uncertainty is clear earlier.
e015	I feel responsible because I conducted the interviews.
e016	This is not just my taste about pacing.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e017	That changes the priority.
e018	If the edit alters how a participant's position is understood, you need to review it against the full interview and the promises you made her, not only against dramatic effect.
e019	You and Jonah may still disagree about how much hesitation belongs in the ending, but the disagreement should be grounded in representation.
e020	A focused re-edit of that thread could be necessary even if the larger structure remains.
[Turn 3 USER]
e021	You moved very quickly to my side.
e022	Jonah has listened to the full interviews too, and the participant approved a cut three months ago.
e023	The current ending is not identical, but it uses the same recorded material.
e024	She also told us she did not want to supervise every edit.
e025	If I contact her whenever I am uncomfortable, I could be shifting authorship onto her and making Jonah feel I use ethics as a veto.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e026	That is fair.
e027	Approval and her wish not to manage the edit are real constraints.
e028	Contacting her is not automatically the respectful option.
e029	You could first compare the approved cut and current ending yourselves, describe the interpretive change without arguing motives, and decide whether it crosses the scope of what she approved.
e030	If you cannot agree, a limited factual or consent question may be better than asking her to adjudicate your artistic conflict.
[Turn 4 USER]
e031	There is history here.
e032	Early on we said major structural decisions would be mutual.
e033	In practice, Jonah made many of them because he was in the session every day, and I usually trusted him.
e034	Now he says I am reopening the structure at the last moment after being less available.
e035	That is partly true.
e036	I was reporting another project for two months.
e037	But I also think “you were not in the room” can turn into permanent final say.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e038	The informal agreement and the working reality diverged.
e039	Jonah accumulated practical authorship through sustained editing, while you did not explicitly surrender mutual authority.
e040	Both facts deserve recognition.
e041	A fair process now may give greater weight to his knowledge of the cut without treating that as unilateral ownership.
e042	The harder question is what mutual decision means under a deadline: consensus on every change, a defined area of final say, or a rule for what happens when you remain split.
[Turn 5 USER]
e043	A curator from the showcase listened yesterday.
e044	She loved the ending and said it was the first time the piece felt inevitable.
e045	That word bothered me, but it also means Jonah achieved something.
e046	She can move us to a later program, though she cannot guarantee the same room or promotion.
e047	Jonah thinks postponing would throw away momentum for a concern the participant may not share.
e048	I am starting to wonder whether I am asking the piece to preserve every ambiguity because I am afraid of making an argument.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e049	Documentaries do make arguments through selection, and preserving every hesitation can be another form of distortion.
e050	The curator's response is useful evidence about the ending's force, not evidence that its interpretation is fair.
e051	The later program reduces the deadline's finality but introduces real opportunity costs.
e052	You might distinguish changes required for representational integrity from changes that would make the argument feel more like yours.
e053	That distinction will not be perfectly objective, but trying to articulate it may clarify the disagreement.
[Turn 6 USER]
e054	Jonah proposed restoring one moment of hesitation and adding a short scene earlier that shows the participant's obligations in the town.
e055	He would keep the final sequence.
e056	I can imagine that working.
e057	But he also wants the credit to read “A film by Jonah Vale and Mira Chen,” even though it is audio, because the showcase uses that language.
e058	I want “Reported by Mira Chen, sound and story by Jonah Vale.” He hears my version as splitting the work into journalism and art.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e059	His edit proposal sounds like a substantive attempt to preserve uncertainty without dissolving the ending, though you should judge it in the cut rather than in description.
e060	The credit disagreement is not merely wording; each version tells a story about what the work is.
e061	Equal top-line authorship plus a second line naming reporting, editing, and sound may acknowledge collaboration and labor, but only if neither of you experiences the top line as erasing the actual imbalance you are trying to name.
[Turn 7 USER]
e062	My provisional plan is to hear Jonah's revised cut before deciding about postponement.
e063	I will compare it with the approved version and write down the exact interpretive difference I still see, if any.
e064	For credit, I will propose equal top-line authorship with detailed role credits below, but I am not sure I can accept that if he still treats structural decisions as his domain.
e065	I want to separate the current film from the rules for our next collaboration, and I am not sure they can really be separated.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e066	Listening before deciding prevents an abstract disagreement from hardening around a cut that does not yet exist.
e067	Your uncertainty about credit and future authority is also legitimate: a current credit can acknowledge completed work, while the feelings behind it may still determine whether you collaborate again.
e068	You do not need to solve the next project before the showcase, but you may need to avoid using a harmonious credit line as evidence that the underlying process felt mutual.
